lots.title: Stockport Town Centre School – Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment
lots.description: Single-lot procurement (Contract Reference 020417) under the Competitive Flexible Procedure to appoint a multi-disciplinary design team for the Stockport Town Centre School project. The roles covered in Stage 1 tender documents are Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, Building Regulations Principal Designer (BR PD) and CDM Principal Designer (CDM PD). This document is the Stage 1 Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) response template; it defines the Stage 1 qualification and technical-ability evaluation framework that candidate suppliers must pass to progress. Lot bidding is confirmed via Question 5 ("Please confirm which lot(s) you wish to bid for?") but no additional lot structure is defined inside this response document.
requirements: Supplier must be registered on the UK Central Digital Platform (CDP) and provide their CDP unique identifier.

Supplier must declare bidding mode (single supplier / group / consortium) and submit up-to-date core supplier information via the CDP covering basic information, economic & financial standing, connected-person information and exclusion grounds.
Supplier must declare any reliance on associated persons (sub-contractors / consortium members that are not guarantors) and disclose them with descriptions and CDP identifiers.
Supplier must declare all intended sub-contractors with unique identifier (or Companies House number / charity number / VAT registration) and a brief description of each intended role.
Supplier must confirm that it is not on the UK Debarment List and that none of its associated persons or intended sub-contractors are on the Debarment List.

Supplier must confirm that it has or can obtain prior to contract award: Employer's (Compulsory) Liability Insurance of £10m, Public Liability Insurance of £10m and Professional Indemnity Insurance of £20m.

Supplier must confirm the human and technical resources in place (or planned by contract award) to comply with UK GDPR and provide a detailed description of data-protection technical facilities and measures.

Supplier must demonstrate relevant experience of designing and delivering school projects on complex, constrained and urban sites, supported by three case studies (≤500 words + 3×250-word case studies with one A4 sheet of project detail each).

Supplier must name each member of the proposed multidisciplinary team covering Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, BR PD and CDM PD, describe how the team will deliver the contract, and provide up to 5 CVs (single A4 per CV) for the key person in each discipline.

Supplier must describe a proposed approach to developing and supporting a viable funding model for the Town Centre School project covering financial challenges/opportunities, funding-option strategy and affordability methodology (≤500 words).
Supplier must demonstrate prior experience of sub-contractor management, supply-chain tracking and prompt-payment practice (e.g., signatory of the UK Prompt Payment Code).
Supplier must confirm systems to pass 30-day payment terms down the supply chain for public-sector contracts awarded under the Procurement Act 2023.
Supplier must confirm a published 2050 Net Zero plan and complete the specified Carbon Reduction Plan Microsoft Forms questionnaire.
Supplier must meet the Modern Slavery Act 2015 Section 54 requirements (or equivalent disclosure if a non-UK supplier) and confirm a list of modern-slavery-related commitments.
Supplier must confirm Real Living Wage (RLW) payment to relevant employees delivering the contract or commit to paying RLW at or above the Living Wage Foundation rate.

Supplier must evidence SSIP (Safety Schemes in Procurement) accreditation within the last 12 months or, failing that, provide evidence against H&S questions (c)-(k) including a written H&S policy, RIDDOR-compliant accident procedures and competent H&S advice.
Supplier must complete the Confirmations declaration attesting that all responses are complete, accurate and not misleading, and provide contact details of the declarant.

It defines the Stage 1 qualification and technical-ability evaluation framework but contains no product-level requirements, quantities or CPV codes. The substantive technical scope lives in sibling documents (e.g. '2-Specification', '7-Stockport-Town-Centre-School-Brief', and the A.1–A.5 scope-of-service documents) which must be extracted separately.
